artifact.note: the packaged jar actually executed; a revision alone does not establish what ran

workload.model: open (constant arrival rate); the generator keeps offering the rate whether or not the application keeps up
workload.authentication: HTTP Basic, enabled; password verification is included in every measured request

dropAttribution.attributedBy: the built-in scenario tag; custom scenario tags do not reach executor-dropped iterations

population.definition: Samples tagged with the measured scenario. Warmup runs as a separate scenario at half rate and none of its samples appear in any figure below.
population.lateCompletionsNote: The window is when work was offered, not when the last response arrived. An iteration starting inside it and finishing after it keeps its measured tag, because k6 lets in-flight iterations finish during graceful stop. An iteration still unfinished when graceful stop ends contributes no sample at all, which is why the sample count can sit slightly below rate x window even with no dropped iterations. Both counts are reported so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

wholeRunIncludingWarmup.note: Reported only so the contaminated aggregate is visible rather than hidden; not a measurement.

asynchronous.recoveryMeans: the broker answered a topic listing again, not merely that the container start command returned
asynchronous.drainedMeans: no unpublished outbox row remains and every payment's projection matches its authoritative status
asynchronous.timeline: per-sample observations with timestamps are in the .backlog.tsv beside this file

telemetry.note: Spans are created at the sampled rate regardless of export. Export off means they are dropped rather than sent.

environment.database: PostgreSQL 16 in Docker, tmpfs storage, fsync=off, max_connections=200, shared_buffers=256MB
environment.broker: Apache Kafka 3.9.1, single node, replication factor 1
environment.applicationHost: same machine as the load generator and the infrastructure containers

limitations: Load generator, application, database and broker share one machine, so they compete for the same CPU.
PostgreSQL runs on tmpfs with fsync off, which flatters write latency and is not a production storage profile.
A single JVM and a single broker node. No replication, no horizontal scaling, no network between tiers.
One run of one workload shape. Percentiles are reported per run and never averaged across runs.
